items.q: In Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics, what does the parameter Km represent?
o: The substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is half of Vmax
The maximum velocity achievable at infinite substrate concentration
The turnover number of substrate molecules per active site per second
The equilibrium constant for the forward chemical reaction
items.exp: Km (the Michaelis constant) is mathematically defined as the substrate concentration [S] at which the initial velocity v0 equals Vmax/2. It serves as an inverse measure of enzyme-substrate affinity.
r: Correct. Km is the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity.
Incorrect. Vmax is the velocity at saturating substrate.
Incorrect. Kcat is the turnover number.
Incorrect. Keq is the thermodynamic equilibrium constant.
items.kp: Km is the substrate concentration required to achieve half-maximal velocity (Vmax/2); a lower Km indicates higher enzyme-substrate affinity.

items.q: How does a reversible competitive inhibitor alter the kinetic parameters of an enzyme on a Lineweaver-Burk double-reciprocal plot?
o: Increases apparent Km (x-intercept shifts closer to origin) while Vmax remains unchanged (y-intercept unchanged)
Decreases Vmax (y-intercept shifts upward) while Km remains unchanged
Decreases both Km and Vmax with parallel lines
items.exp: Competitive inhibitors compete with substrate for the active site. Saturating substrate concentrations displace the inhibitor, reaching normal Vmax (1/Vmax unchanged). However, higher substrate is needed, raising apparent Km (-1/Km shifts toward 0).
r: Correct. Competitive inhibitors increase apparent Km while leaving Vmax unchanged.
Incorrect. Lowering Vmax with unchanged Km describes noncompetitive inhibition.
Incorrect. Decreasing both Km and Vmax describes uncompetitive inhibition.
Incorrect. This combination does not occur in simple reversible inhibition.
items.kp: Competitive inhibitors increase apparent Km without changing Vmax; on Lineweaver-Burk plots, lines intersect on the y-axis at 1/Vmax.

items.q: Statins (e.g., atorvastatin) reduce plasma LDL cholesterol by acting as which kinetic class of inhibitor against HMG-CoA reductase?
items.exp: Statins possess a bulky hydrophobic group and a dihydroxyheptanoic acid moiety structurally mimicking the HMG intermediate of HMG-CoA, competitively binding the catalytic active site of HMG-CoA reductase.
r: Correct. Statins are structural analogues that competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase.
Incorrect. Suicide inhibitors covalently inactivate enzymes irreversibly (e.g., aspirin on COX-1).
Incorrect. Noncompetitive inhibitors bind allosteric sites.
Incorrect. Uncompetitive inhibitors bind only the ES complex.
items.kp: Statins are competitive reversible inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, structurally mimicking the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl substrate.

author_self_check.note: Hand-authored and verified against standard references

x.key: Statins are competitive reversible inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, structurally mimicking the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl substrate.
x.pearl: Statins are competitive reversible inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, structurally mimicking the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl substrate.

items.q: How does a noncompetitive (allosteric) inhibitor alter the kinetic parameters of an enzyme?
o: Decreases both Km and Vmax proportionally
items.exp: Noncompetitive inhibitors bind an allosteric site on both free enzyme and enzyme-substrate complex with equal affinity. Because they do not compete with substrate, Km is unchanged; however, they impair catalysis, lowering Vmax.
r: Correct. Pure noncompetitive inhibitors decrease Vmax while keeping Km constant.
Incorrect. Increasing Km with unchanged Vmax is competitive inhibition.
Incorrect. Decreasing both proportionally is uncompetitive inhibition.
Incorrect. This is not observed in noncompetitive inhibition.
items.kp: Noncompetitive inhibitors decrease Vmax without changing Km; on Lineweaver-Burk plots, lines intersect on the x-axis at -1/Km.

items.q: Aspirin exerts its antiplatelet effect for the entire 7 to 10 day lifespan of circulating platelets through which mechanism?
o: Irreversible covalent acetylation of a serine residue (Ser-529) in the active site of cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1)
Allosteric noncompetitive inhibition of thromboxane synthase
items.exp: Aspirin transfers its acetyl group to Ser-529 in platelet COX-1, permanently blocking arachidonic acid access. Because anucleate platelets cannot synthesize new protein, COX-1 remains inactivated for the platelet's lifespan.
r: Correct. Aspirin covalently acetylates Ser-529 in COX-1 irreversibly.
Incorrect. Aspirin's antiplatelet action is irreversible and primarily targets COX-1.
Incorrect. It does not inhibit thromboxane synthase directly.
Incorrect. Cilostazol inhibits PDE-3, not aspirin.
items.kp: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates Ser-529 in platelet COX-1, permanently abolishing thromboxane A2 production for the 7-10 day lifespan of the platelet.

items.q: Why does hepatic glucokinase (hexokinase IV) possess a high Km (~10 mM) compared to extrahepatic hexokinase I (Km <0.1 mM)?
o: Enables the liver to clear glucose and synthesize glycogen only when portal blood glucose is high after meals
Ensures the liver traps all glucose during fasting hypoglycemia
Prevents the liver from synthesizing fatty acids
Allows hepatocytes to export glucose-6-phosphate directly into blood
items.exp: Glucokinase has a high Km (~10 mM) corresponding to postprandial portal glucose concentrations. It is not inhibited by glucose-6-phosphate, allowing hepatocytes to remove large glucose loads after meals without saturating.
r: Correct. High Km ensures glucokinase phosphorylates glucose primarily during postprandial hyperglycemia.
Incorrect. Extrahepatic hexokinase has low Km to trap glucose during fasting.
Incorrect. Glucokinase promotes fatty acid synthesis from excess glucose.
Incorrect. G6P must be hydrolyzed by G6Pase to exit hepatocytes.
items.kp: Hepatic glucokinase has a high Km (~10 mM) and lacks product inhibition, functioning as a postprandial glucose sensor and gatekeeper for glycogen and lipid synthesis.

items.q: In an uncompetitive inhibition model, the inhibitor binds exclusively to which species, causing parallel lines on a Lineweaver-Burk plot?
o: Both free enzyme and ES complex with equal affinity
items.exp: Uncompetitive inhibitors bind only to the enzyme-substrate complex. This shifts the equilibrium to favor substrate binding (decreasing apparent Km) while inactivating the complex (decreasing Vmax) by the same ratio, producing parallel lines.
r: Correct. Uncompetitive inhibitors bind exclusively to the ES complex, reducing both Km and Vmax.
Incorrect. Binding free enzyme only is competitive inhibition.
Incorrect. Binding both equally is pure noncompetitive inhibition.
Incorrect. Product inhibition is distinct.
items.kp: Uncompetitive inhibitors bind exclusively to the enzyme-substrate (ES) complex, decreasing both Km and Vmax proportionally and yielding parallel Lineweaver-Burk lines.

items.q: What kinetic term represents the catalytic efficiency of an enzyme, accounting for both substrate affinity and catalytic turnover?
items.exp: The specificity constant, defined as Kcat / Km, reflects catalytic efficiency at low substrate concentrations, measuring both how rapidly the enzyme turns over substrate (Kcat) and how well it binds (1/Km).
r: Correct. Kcat/Km is the specificity constant defining overall catalytic efficiency.
Incorrect. Vmax/Km reflects initial slope but depends on enzyme concentration.
Incorrect. 1/Km reflects only affinity.
Incorrect. Km/Kcat is the reciprocal.
items.kp: Catalytic efficiency is measured by the specificity constant Kcat/Km, representing the rate of catalytic turnover relative to substrate affinity.

items.q: Allosteric enzymes typically display which type of velocity-versus-substrate curve, reflecting cooperative subunit interactions rather than simple Michaelis-Menten kinetics?
items.exp: Allosteric enzymes with multiple interacting catalytic subunits (e.g., PFK-1, aspartate transcarbamoylase) exhibit sigmoidal (S-shaped) saturation curves due to positive or negative cooperativity.
r: Correct. Allosteric enzymes display sigmoidal velocity curves due to cooperativity.
Incorrect. Hyperbolic curves characterize non-cooperative Michaelis-Menten enzymes.
Incorrect. Linear curves indicate zero-order or simple first-order ranges.
Incorrect. Logarithmic curves do not represent raw velocity plots.
items.kp: Allosteric enzymes display sigmoidal (S-shaped) substrate saturation curves reflecting cooperative transitions between tense and relaxed states.

items.q: A Lineweaver-Burk plot of an enzymatic reaction reveals an x-intercept of -0.2 mM^-1 and a y-intercept of 0.05 (micromol/min)^-1. What are the Km and Vmax of this enzyme?
items.exp: x-intercept = -1/Km = -0.2 mM^-1 -> Km = 1 / 0.2 = 5.0 mM. y-intercept = 1/Vmax = 0.05 -> Vmax = 1 / 0.05 = 20 micromol/min.
r: Correct. Km = -1/(-0.2) = 5.0 mM; Vmax = 1/0.05 = 20 micromol/min.
Incorrect. These are the un-inverted raw intercept values.
Incorrect. Mathematical calculation error.
Incorrect. Vmax was not inverted.
items.kp: On Lineweaver-Burk plots, Km equals -1 divided by the x-intercept, and Vmax equals 1 divided by the y-intercept.
